description: Official and institutional documents the planner's assistant retrieves from (RAG): poultry schemes, NABARD and NCDC projects, CPCB and DAHD rules, and the TNAU and Vikaspedia poultry guides. Each entry is downloaded and converted to plain text by datasets/scripts/fetch_knowledge.py. The text itself is not committed (some sources are copyrighted); only this list is.

sources.title: National Livestock Mission, Entrepreneurship Development Programme guidelines 2021-26 (revised August 2024)
sources.publisher: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (copy hosted by the Kerala Livestock Development Board)
sources.note: The only capital subsidy for poultry: 50% back-ended, capped at Rs 25 lakh, for a rural poultry parent farm with hatchery and brooder-mother unit. It does not cover a plain broiler or layer farm.

sources.title: Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) guidelines
sources.publisher: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (copy hosted by GADVASU)
sources.note: 3% interest subvention on loans for feed plants and meat processing, not for the farm itself.

sources.title: NABARD unit costs 2023-24 (Jharkhand Regional Office), including poultry farming
sources.publisher: NABARD
sources.scope: Jharkhand (NABARD unit costs are set per state)
sources.note: Bank unit costs for broiler and layer units. Other states publish their own; the figures differ.

sources.title: NABARD unit costs 2025-26 (Maharashtra Regional Office, SLUCC 21 March 2025), including poultry
sources.publisher: NABARD
sources.scope: Maharashtra (NABARD unit costs are set per state)
sources.note: Broiler (own and contract, open and controlled), layer cage and Kaveri units. Used by the Cost step's NABARD card for Maharashtra projects.

sources.title: NABARD unit costs 2026-27 (Tamil Nadu & UT of Puducherry Regional Office, June 2026), including poultry
sources.publisher: NABARD (copy hosted by the State Level Bankers' Committee, Tamil Nadu)
sources.scope: Tamil Nadu and Puducherry (NABARD unit costs are set per state)
sources.note: Broiler 5,000-20,000 birds, standalone and integrated (1+1+7) cage layers 10,000-1,00,000 birds, hybrid and other poultry, quail. Used by the Cost step's NABARD card for Tamil Nadu projects.

sources.title: Maharashtra GR DAHD-14017/1/2026-AH4, 9 March 2026: Mukhyamantri Gramin Pashudhan Udyojakta Yojana, State Plan Scheme (in Marathi)
sources.publisher: Government of Maharashtra, Agriculture, Dairy Development, Animal Husbandry and Fisheries Department
sources.note: The state's poultry subsidy: 50% (75% SC/ST) of a fixed project cost for 5,000 layers (Rs 30 lakh) or 3,000 or 5,000 desi or improved meat birds (Rs 12 or 19 lakh); also a hatchery unit and a 4% interest subvention. Used by the Cost step's scheme card for Maharashtra projects.

sources.title: Corrigendum of 27 August 2026 to Maharashtra GR DAHD-14017/1/2026-AH4, State Plan Scheme (in Marathi)
sources.publisher: Government of Maharashtra, Agriculture, Dairy Development, Animal Husbandry and Fisheries Department
sources.note: Changes the dairy unit and the loan-repayment wording, and moves selection from a random draw to first come, first served. Nothing changes for poultry.

sources.title: Bihar Directorate of Animal Husbandry letter 1957 of 23 May 2025, under sanction order 6 SS(6)13/2023-2195 of 20 May 2025
sources.publisher: Government of Bihar
sources.note: Bihar: subsidy for a broiler farm of 3,000 birds (Saat Nishchay-2). A 3,000-bird broiler unit costs Rs 10,00,000: 30% (up to Rs 3,00,000) for general applicants, 50% (up to Rs 5,00,000) for SC/ST.

sources.title: Bihar Directorate of Animal Husbandry letter 1958 of 23 May 2025, under sanction order 6 SS(6)40/2014(Khand)-2200 of 20 May 2025
sources.publisher: Government of Bihar
sources.note: Bihar: Samekit Murgi Vikas Yojana (layer farm). 5,000 layers cost Rs 48,50,000 and 10,000 layers Rs 1,00,00,000; the subsidy is 30% for general applicants and 40% for SC/ST.

sources.title: Odisha Directorate of AH&VS, guidelines for broiler farming 2026-27, file PT1-AHVS-PD-MISC-0048-2025/01/2026 (May 2026)
sources.publisher: Government of Odisha
sources.note: Odisha: support to farmers for broiler farming (State Plan, 2026-27). Units of 2,000, 2,500 and 3,000 birds cost Rs 7.2, 9.0 and 10.8 lakh. Paid after the work is done, in two halves.

sources.title: Odisha Directorate of AH&VS, guidelines for layer farming 2026-27, file PT1-AHVS-PD-MISC-0048-2025/01/2026 (May 2026)
sources.publisher: Government of Odisha
sources.note: Odisha: support to farmers for layer farming (State Plan, 2026-27). Rs 8.225 lakh per 1,000 layers, in cages or on deep litter, for 1,000 to 4,000 birds. Paid after the work is done, in two halves.

sources.title: Uttarakhand GO 1631/XV-1/22-1(15)/2022 of 15 Nov 2022, continued in 2025-26 by GO 1768/XV-1/2025/87507 of 19 Sep 2025
sources.publisher: Government of Uttarakhand
sources.note: Uttarakhand: establishment of broiler farms. A 500-bird unit costs Rs 3,05,100. The subsidy is a fixed Rs 60,000: Rs 15 a bird for 6 batches plus Rs 15,000 for the shed.

sources.title: Uttarakhand GO 588/XV-1/25/62949 of 9 Jun 2025 (policy, to 31 Dec 2030); procedure GO 2014/XV-1/2025-93015 of 10 Oct 2025
sources.publisher: Government of Uttarakhand
sources.note: Uttarakhand Poultry Development Policy 2025 (commercial layer farm). Plains: 30,000 layers, Rs 1.8 crore, 30% up to Rs 54 lakh. Hills: 15,000 layers, Rs 1.2 crore, 40% up to Rs 48 lakh. Paid 50%, 40% and 10% as the farm comes up.

sources.title: Uttar Pradesh policy GO 2254/37-2-2022-1(45)/2012TC of 7 Nov 2022; implementing GO 2505/37-2-2022-1(45)/12TC of 29 Dec 2022
sources.publisher: Government of Uttar Pradesh
sources.note: Uttar Pradesh Poultry Development Policy 2022: interest reimbursement for a layer farm. 7% interest reimbursed for 5 years on units of 10,000, 30,000 or 60,000 caged layers (Rs 99.53, 256.69 and 491.90 lakh), up to Rs 14.61, 37.71 and 72.30 lakh.

sources.title: Assam notification VFV.38/2024/1 of 16 Mar 2024, amended by ECF.No. 670980/60 (cited as 3 Nov 2025)
sources.publisher: Government of Assam
sources.note: Assam: Policy for Commercialisation of Poultry Sector 2024 (amended 2025). 33% of the capital cost, up to Rs 5 crore, for layer farms of 50,000+ birds and broiler farms of 20,000+, paid 20/40/40 as the farm reaches 20%, 40% and 90% of capacity.

sources.title: NABARD model bankable project: broiler farming
sources.publisher: NABARD (copy hosted by TNAU Agritech)
sources.note: The structure of the planner's broiler project (batches, cleaning days, mortality). Its prices are old; use the unit costs and the planner's figures for money.

sources.title: NABARD model bankable project: commercial layer farming
sources.publisher: NABARD (copy hosted by TNAU Agritech)
sources.note: Layer house space, grower and laying periods, egg numbers. Its prices are old.

sources.title: NABARD model project: indigenous (desi) poultry farming
sources.publisher: NABARD
sources.note: Backyard and low-cost sheds for improved desi birds.

sources.title: NCDC sample detailed project report: broiler farming
sources.publisher: National Cooperative Development Corporation
sources.note: Sale weight and feed per bird used by the planner.

sources.title: CPCB Environmental Guidelines for Poultry Farms
sources.publisher: Central Pollution Control Board (page on India Environment Portal)
sources.note: Consent above 5,000 birds and siting distances, enforced by NGT orders of 2020 and 2021. The page summarises the guideline; the full text is the CPCB PDF.

sources.title: General guidelines on biosecurity in poultry farms (revised August 2015)
sources.publisher: Department of Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries (released through PIB)
sources.note: Farm location, restricted access, quarantine, cleaning, personnel hygiene, manure, dead birds and feed safety. Written for central farms and meant to be applied by state and private farms too.

sources.title: TNAU Agritech poultry expert system: poultry house construction
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU Agritech Portal)
sources.note: Shed width, eaves and centre height, overhang, floor space. The planner's shed sizes follow it.

sources.title: TNAU Agritech poultry expert system: broiler management
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU Agritech Portal)
sources.note: Brooding, feeding, water and management of broilers.

sources.title: TNAU Agritech poultry expert system: layer management
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU Agritech Portal)
sources.note: Management of laying hens.

sources.title: TNAU Agritech poultry expert system: grower management
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU Agritech Portal)
sources.note: Feeding and management of growing pullets.

sources.title: TNAU Agritech poultry expert system: brooding of chicks
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU Agritech Portal)
sources.note: Brooder temperatures and chick care.

sources.title: TNAU Agritech poultry expert system: litter management
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU Agritech Portal)
sources.note: Deep litter depth and care.

sources.title: TNAU Agritech poultry expert system: poultry farm equipment
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU Agritech Portal)
sources.note: Feeders, drinkers, brooders and cages.

sources.title: TNAU Agritech poultry expert system: lighting
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU Agritech Portal)
sources.note: Light hours and placement for broilers and layers.

sources.title: TNAU Agritech poultry expert system: disease control and vaccination
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU Agritech Portal)
sources.note: Diseases and vaccination schedules. Doses and medicines are for a veterinarian to decide.

sources.title: TNAU Agritech poultry expert system: biosecurity
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU Agritech Portal)
sources.note: Farm biosecurity practice.

sources.title: Vikaspedia: broiler production
sources.publisher: Vikaspedia (Government of India, MeitY / C-DAC)
sources.note: Brooding temperatures, floor space, health care and marketing for broilers.

sources.title: Vikaspedia: poultry layer farming
sources.publisher: Vikaspedia (Government of India, MeitY / C-DAC)
sources.note: A model layer project: housing, cages, feeding and economics.

gaps: There is no central capital subsidy for a plain commercial broiler or layer farm; NLM-EDP covers rural poultry parent farms only. State schemes vary and are not in the knowledge base apart from the rules in the planner's scheme table.
NABARD unit costs are included for Jharkhand only; other states' unit costs differ.
IS 2732:1985 (poultry housing) is not freely available; its figures come through the TNAU expert system.
No official source gives daily market prices for broilers or eggs; the planner's prices are assumptions the farmer can change.
Medicine and vaccine doses are for a veterinarian; the sources give schedules, not prescriptions.

The CPCB guideline itself (the PDF circulated to the state boards) is not in the knowledge base, only the India Environment Portal summary of the NGT orders; its siting distances are in the planner's siting table (datasets/csv/poultry_siting_rules.csv).
